statements.statement: I2C lines use pull-up resistors to keep SDA and SCL HIGH by default.
statements.explanation: Both SDA and SCL use pull-up resistors to keep them HIGH by default. When a device wants to transmit, it pulls the line LOW.

statements.statement: In the open-drain design of I2C, devices can both push a line HIGH and pull it LOW.
statements.explanation: In an open-drain design, devices can only pull a line LOW, never push it up. The pull-up resistor handles returning the line to HIGH.

statements.statement: The open-drain design allows multiple I2C devices to safely share the same two wires without electrically conflicting.
statements.explanation: Because devices can only pull lines LOW (never push HIGH), multiple devices can share SDA and SCL without electrically fighting each other.
